new_page.title: Coquitlam Neighbourhood Guides | 23 Areas | Jared Gibbons
new_page.description: Compare all 23 Coquitlam neighbourhoods: what sold in each in the last 12 months, median prices by home type and a guide page for each. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Figures are closed sales from Jared’s Paragon export; the neighbourhood map outlines are drawn by us and stay draft until each is confirmed.

Coquitlam is split into 23 MLS® sub-areas, the neighbourhood boundaries the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® board uses for every listing and sale. From November 2025 to October 22, 2026, 1,613 homes sold across them: 470 houses, 768 condos and 307 townhomes and 57 duplexes. The busiest were Coquitlam West (485), Burke Mountain (210), North Coquitlam (198).

By median price, the houses that sold in Burke Mountain were the most expensive of the 12 Coquitlam neighbourhoods with 10 or more house sales ($1,954,000), and those in New Horizons the least ($1,200,000). For condos, the range ran from $426,250 in Central Coquitlam to $695,000 in New Horizons.

These are MLS® sub-areas, not the City of Coquitlam’s planning areas, so a neighbourhood here can be larger or smaller than the name suggests. The map and tables below follow the board’s boundaries. Use them to compare areas, then ask Jared for a search set to the exact streets you care about.

blocks.source: Source: Paragon, the MLS® system used by Jared’s office, closed sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026. Pending sales are not counted. Median means the middle price, so half sold for more and half for less. Sold vs list is the sale price as a percentage of the last list price. A figure is shown only where at least 5 homes sold, and a median is shown only with 5 or more sales; with fewer, one sale would be the whole figure.

blocks.text: Westwood Summit has fewer than 10 closed sales in the period, too few for a page of figures, so they appear in the tables only.

faq.q: How many neighbourhoods does Coquitlam have?
faq.a: The MLS® splits Coquitlam into 23 sub-areas: Burke Mountain, Canyon Springs, Cape Horn, Central Coquitlam, Chineside, Coquitlam East and 17 more. 22 have a page on this site.

faq.q: Which Coquitlam neighbourhood sold the most homes?
faq.a: Coquitlam West had the most closed sales, 485 between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, followed by Burke Mountain (210) and North Coquitlam (198).

faq.q: Where are Coquitlam houses the most and least expensive?
faq.a: Among areas with 10 or more house sales, the median was highest in Burke Mountain at $1,954,000 and lowest in New Horizons at $1,200,000, for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Which Coquitlam neighbourhoods are best value for a condo?
faq.a: Median condo prices ran from $426,250 in Central Coquitlam to $695,000 in New Horizons among areas with 10 or more condo sales. Price is one measure only; compare strata fees, age and building condition too.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Coquitlam?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Coquitlam?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.
